rationale: Minimal local-first approach. Hash chain detects line modification/deletion/insertion/reordering. Checkpoints provide batch verification roots. No external dependencies.
Blockchain introduces consensus/network/operational overhead unjustified for local dogfood. Hash chain + checkpoint records provide sufficient tamper evidence for v0.1-v0.6.
Linear hash chain suffices for single-host tamper detection. Merkle inclusion proofs add implementation complexity with no benefit until external verification/sharing matters.
Avoids mixing schemas in a single file. Checkpoints have different schema_version, required fields, and lifecycle. Separate file simplifies reader logic.
1000-event window balances I/O overhead with detection granularity. Explicit checkpoint() call allows on-demand checkpointing before risky operations.
Fast, well-supported, already used elsewhere in codebase (receipt_envelope.py, execution_request.py, coordination hashes). No need for a different algorithm.
Existing deterministic sorted-keyed JSON serializer in rig_relay.coordination._canonical_json. No need to implement a new canonical form.
Enables per-event integrity check without recomputing hashes from scratch on every read. Nullable for backward compatibility with existing events.
Standard hash chain pattern. Null is unambiguous for the first event. Python Pydantic optional string field naturally supports this.
Existing events without event_hash/previous_event_hash remain valid. On read, unhashed events are skipped during verification rather than rejected.
Automatic repair would destroy tamper evidence. The store must report breaks and let the user decide on recovery (export up to break, start new chain from last valid checkpoint).
First broken link invalidates all subsequent chain hashes. Reporting 'unverifiable' rather than 'failed' for subsequent events is more accurate.
Store-level methods (append, read_events, create_checkpoint, verify) suffice for programmatic verification. CLI is a thin wrapper that can be added later.
Requires keychain module (macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service, Windows Credential Manager) and signing infrastructure (Ed25519). Not needed for local dogfood.
NIST SP 800-92 separates log storage, integrity checking, retention, analysis, and disposal. Current design addresses integrity checking only. Retention/disposal policies are deferred.
CT-style Merkle inclusion proofs and consistency proofs add complexity. Defer until external verification/sharing matters.
Current malformed-line tolerance is correct. Chain verification stops at the malformed line. Future repair workflow can quarantine lines and splice.
next_sequence() remains a count of lines. Hash chain adds detection of gaps and duplicates: a missing sequence breaks the chain; two events claiming the same parent produce a fork.

ReceiptEnvelope is separate from tamper evidence. The audit trail stores AuditEvent records which may embed ReceiptEnvelope. The hash chain operates on AuditEvent canonical JSON, which covers embedded envelopes. Standalone envelopes need their own integrity mechanism.
Phased implementation reduces risk. Each phase is independently testable. Phase 0.1+0.2 = minimum viable tamper evidence (hash chain + checkpoints). Phases 0.3-0.6 add CLI and external anchoring.
